t: Mendoza's settlement of 1536 was abandoned after attacks by indigenous people, and Garay's refounding of 1580 became a port that depended on trade and, under Spanish restrictions, on contraband.

The city became the capital of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata, began Argentina's independence with the May Revolution of 1810, and was federalised in 1880 as the seat of the national government.
From 1880 to 1930 it received millions of immigrants, mostly from Italy and Spain, and in the 1970s it suffered political violence and the military dictatorship that began in 1976.
dyk: The name came from the Virgin of Buen Ayre, the Madonna of Bonaria in Cagliari, Sardinia, whom Spanish sailors invoked for fair winds; for many years it was wrongly attributed to a Sancho del Campo, until Eduardo Madero's research in 1882.
ev: Pedro de Mendoza establishes the first settlement, in what is now the San Telmo district
Juan de Garay founds the permanent settlement
Charles III declares Buenos Aires an open port and makes it capital of the new Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata
The May Revolution removes the viceroy Cisneros and begins the Argentine War of Independence
The city is federalised and becomes the seat of government
The demonstration of 17 October at the Plaza de Mayo marks the emergence of Peronism
A coup led by General Jorge Videla begins the military dictatorship
The city elects its first head of government, after the constitutional amendment of 1994 gave it autonomy

f.founded: Established on 2 February 1536 by a Spanish expedition led by Pedro de Mendoza and abandoned in the early 1540s; a second and permanent settlement was founded on 11 June 1580 by Juan de Garay, who came down the Paraná River from Asunción.
f.where: On the south-western shore of the Río de la Plata, in the pampa region of Argentina.
f.known: The port of the Río de la Plata; the capital of the Viceroyalty of the Río de la Plata; the May Revolution of 1810; waves of European immigration from 1880 to 1930; the Plaza de Mayo; tango; the dictatorship of 1976 to 1983 and the Mothers of the Plaza de Mayo
f.today: Buenos Aires is the capital of Argentina and an autonomous city, neither part of Buenos Aires Province nor its capital.
